title: Safe Transfer, Steady Hands

patient.name: Mr Rajoo s/o Krishnan
patient.presenting_complaint: Attending the injection clinic for his regular eye injection; uses a wheelchair after a stroke and needs help to move to the examination chair

history.hpc: Mr Rajoo comes for his scheduled intravitreal injection review. He had a stroke two years ago with left-sided weakness and uses a wheelchair, but can stand briefly with support. He says: 'My leg not so strong after the stroke, cannot stand long, must hold something.' He is alert and cooperative. He needs to transfer from his wheelchair to the examination chair for assessment.
history.pmhx: Previous stroke with left hemiparesis. Diabetes, hypertension. Wet AMD (right eye) on anti-VEGF injections.
history.social_hx: Lives with wife and son. Wheelchair user, son pushes him to appointments. Son is parking the car.

examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: known wet AMD changes (for doctor review). Left eye: to be assessed.

investigations.fall_risk_assessment: High risk: elderly, post-stroke left-sided weakness, wheelchair-dependent with limited standing ability, reduced vision (RE 6/60), and requires assisted transfer. Companion (son) temporarily absent.

diagnosis: High fall risk during transfer due to post-stroke weakness, wheelchair dependence, and reduced vision. The key safety task is a safe assisted transfer and continuous supervision, not just documentation.

immediate: Recognise that all patients are assessed for fall risk each visit, and this patient is high risk for falls during transfer
Do not attempt the transfer alone if unsafe — get a second staff member to assist and use the wheelchair brakes
Position the wheelchair correctly, lock the brakes, and guide the patient to stand and pivot with support to the examination chair
Keep the patient supervised at all times; do not leave him standing or transferring unaccompanied
Wait for or call the son to return, and ensure the patient is escorted for the rest of the visit
Document the fall risk assessment and the action taken (assisted transfer, brakes locked, supervised, son informed)
follow_up: Doctor to proceed with the injection review for the right eye
Ensure assisted transfer back to the wheelchair after the procedure
Flag in records that this patient needs assisted transfer and an escort at every visit
patient_education: Explain each step before moving him so he is not startled and can help safely
Advise him to tell staff before trying to stand or move so help is on hand
Reassure him that staff will assist with every transfer
Encourage him to attend with his son or a companion for safety

key_points: Establishes the post-stroke weakness and limited standing ability
Confirms wheelchair dependence and the need for an assisted transfer
Notes the reduced vision (RE 6/60) as an added risk factor
Checks whether a companion is present (son temporarily away)
Performs and documents a fall risk assessment at this visit
Identifies the specific transfer-related risk factors (weakness, wheelchair, reduced vision)
Recognises that the highest-risk moment is the transfer itself
Classifies the patient as high fall risk
Recognises that assisted transfer with supervision is required
Understands that high risk requires active measures, not just a note
Does not assume the patient can transfer independently
Gets help and uses wheelchair brakes for a safe, supervised transfer
Never leaves the patient unsupervised during standing/transfer
Documents the fall risk assessment and the actions taken
Communicates the need for an escort and flags it for future visits
